subject: points w/ solid outline filled w/ colour gradient

messages.author: 34b9db55c3269f28
messages.subject: points w/ solid outline filled w/ colour gradient
parts:
Dear ggplot2ers,

In the following example, I would like to have all points have a
solid, non-transparent black outline, and be filled with some
transparency graded from black to white corresponding to values of z:


library(ggplot2)
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- rnorm(100)
z <- sample(-3:3,100,replace=TRUE)
df <- data.frame(x=x,y=y,z=z)

# the following produces hollow point symbols (which I thought were
# "shape = 1") with the outline in colour_gradient:
ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y = y, colour=z)) + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, shape = 21) + scale_colour_gradient(low = "black", high = "white")

# this gives: "Error in grid.pretty(range) : 'range' must be numeric"
ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y = y, colour=z)) + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, shape = 21) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white")

Many thanks for any pointers.

Marianne

--
Marianne Promberger PhD, King's College London

ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y = y, fill=z)) + geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6,

shape = 21) +
scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white")

Using fill indeed makes it work -- thanks! But the alpha gets applied to the
point outline instead of the fill. See this example which should give
a bit of overplotting and make this visible:

library(ggplot2)
x <- sample(-1:1,1000,replace=TRUE)
y <- sample(-1:1,1000,replace=TRUE)
z <- sample(-3:3,1000,replace=TRUE)
df <- data.frame(x=x,y=y,z=z)
ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y = y, fill=z)) + geom_jitter(alpha = .2 , shape = 21) + scale_fill_gradient(low = "black", high = "white")

Marianne

messages.subject: RE: points w/ solid outline filled w/ colour gradient
parts:
Hi Marianne,

Not quite elegant, but worked for me:

library(ggplot2)
x <- sample(-1:1, 100, replace = TRUE)
y <- sample(-1:1, 100, replace = TRUE)
z <- sample(-3:3, 100, replace = TRUE)
b <- rep("black", 100)
nz <- (z + 3) / 6
df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y, z = z, b = b, nz = nz)
pdf("biorrame.pdf")
ggplot(df,aes(x=x, y = y, fill = alpha(b, nz))) +
geom_jitter(shape = 21, size = 20) +
scale_fill_identity()

Probably the ideal solution involves scale_alpha (the effect indeed is quite
similar), although I was not able to retain solid borders ...

Hope this helps, best,
fernando
